newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to try three in Sadat widow case.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to try three in Sadat widow case.

text.p: Egypt's prosecutor general on Thursday ordered the trial of three men including an opposition newspaper editor and reporter for forging a birth certificate that said one of them fathered a child with the widow of the late president Anwar Sadat.
The case is based on a story that the opposition newspaper al-Ahrar carried in August on the ease with which official documents could be forged in Egypt.

Reporter Ahmed Fikry Abdel-Hamid is alleged to have paid registry clerk Gamal Zaki Garas 20 pounds ($6) to issue him a birth certificate that named Abdel-Hamid as the father and Sadat's widow Jihan as the mother.
Mostafa Bakry, the editor of the paper at the time, and Abdel-Hamid will stand trial on charges of invading and abusing the privacy of the Sadat family.
Abdel-Hamid also faces charges of bribing a state employee while Garas is charged with accepting it.
The newspaper is the mouthpiece of the opposition Ahrar party. The party's leader Mostafa Kamel Murad fired Bakry after the public outcry that followed the article's publication.
A date has not been set for the trial, which will be in a Higher State Security court.
The prosecutor general on Thursday also referred Bakry to stand trial in a criminal court for libelling former religious endowments minister Mohammed al-Mahgoub.
